metaDescription: Six curtain sets at or under $100 compared on length, fabric weight, blackout weave, header style and width, with honest notes on what the higher cap buys.
expertTake: The NICETOWN 340 gsm blackout set is the best overall pick because its stated heavy fabric weight and thermal lining give the most substance at this cap. The H.VERSAILTEX 108 inch double-wide panel is the pick for tall windows and sliding doors. Skip off-the-shelf curtains under any cap if your window is unusually wide or tall and you need custom width, because panels that are too narrow look flat and leak light.
introParagraphs: Curtains do four jobs: they block light, soften the room, add privacy and take the edge off drafts and echo. At a higher cap than the entry tier you can buy more length, a heavier fabric and better headers, and that is where this guide spends its attention.

A larger budget still has limits. Ready-made panels come in fixed widths and lengths, and a ready-made blackout is only as good as its weave and the way you hang it. We compare the options by fabric weight, size and how well each handles gaps at the sides and the top.

products.name: NICETOWN 340 GSM Thermal Blackout Curtains, 84 Inch, Black
products.description:
NICETOWN lists a fabric weight of 340 gsm per panel and says that is 60 percent heavier than ordinary blackout curtains. Fabric weight is a rough measure of body: heavier panels hang straighter, block more light and dampen sound a little better. The listing also calls them thermal insulated, which means a lined fabric that slows heat loss, not a substitute for window sealing.

A heavy panel needs a sturdy rod. Standard 1 inch rods bow past about 48 inches, so add a center bracket for wide windows. Compared with the Simplebrand at 280 gsm, the NICETOWN is noticeably heavier, but also stiffer, so it takes longer to relax into folds after unboxing. The listing does not state grommet size in the data reviewed.

Hang the rod 4 to 6 inches above the frame and extend it 3 to 6 inches past each side so the glass is clear. Wash on gentle and air dry, since heat can damage coatings. Steam wrinkles from the fabric rather than ironing the lining. If the room faces west, the lining also takes some of the afternoon glare off a television or a bed, which is where heavier panels earn their place.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms and media rooms that need real weight, darkness and some thermal benefit.
pros: 340 gsm fabric weight hangs straighter and blocks more light than thin panels
Thermal lining slows heat loss at a cold window
Solid black reads as a deep, dark backdrop in a media room
Two panels per set cover a standard window with some fullness
cons: Heavy fabric needs a sturdy rod and a center support on wide windows
Stiff weave takes days to relax into soft folds after unboxing

products.badge: Best for Tall or Wide Windows
products.name: H.VERSAILTEX 108 Inch Blackout Linen Look Grommet Curtain, 100 Inch Wide
products.description:
H.VERSAILTEX offers a single panel that is 100 inches wide and 108 inches long, with grommets and a faux linen face over a blackout backing. A double-wide panel suits a sliding door, a picture window or a tall ceiling where two standard panels would leave a visible gap in the middle. The listing cites a Global Recycled Standard certificate for the fabric.

One wide panel avoids the center gap but is heavy to slide, and you need a rod strong enough to carry it without bending. Compared with the NICETOWN, the H.VERSAILTEX is a single panel with a linen texture, so it looks softer but wrinkles more. The 108 inch length suits a high ceiling mount, though the data reviewed does not state a fabric weight.

Support the rod with at least three brackets. Grommets glide easily, which helps with a wide panel. Wash gently, air dry, and steam out creases. Keep the hem about half an inch above the floor so it does not drag. Because one panel serves the whole opening, stack space on one side matters, so allow room on the wall beside the door for the folded fabric.
products.bestFor: Sliding doors and tall windows that need one wide, long panel.
pros: 100 inch width covers a sliding door without a middle gap
108 inch length reaches the floor from a high ceiling mount
Grommets let a heavy panel glide along the rod
Faux linen face looks soft and casual in daylight
cons: A single wide panel is heavy to slide and needs strong brackets
Fabric weight is not stated in the data reviewed

products.name: H.VERSAILTEX 84 Inch Blackout Linen Look Curtains, Ivory Pair
products.description:
H.VERSAILTEX sells an ivory pair of 52 by 84 inch panels, 104 inches wide in total, in a faux linen with a white blackout coating. The listing cites the Global Recycled Standard for the fabric and calls the finish room darkening and thermal.

Light colors with a blackout coating are a good compromise: the coating blocks light, while the ivory face keeps the room from feeling heavy. The trade is that coatings crack if overheated, so wash on gentle and air dry. Compared with the 108 inch panel, the pair is lighter and easier to hang, and it fits a standard window with a decent amount of fullness.

A 104 inch pair width suits a window about 50 to 70 inches wide, which gives 1.5 to 2 times fullness. Hang it wide and high. The data reviewed does not state fabric weight, so keep expectations for thermal benefit modest. Ivory shows dust marks less than white but more than gray, so plan a gentle vacuum pass along the bottom hem every few weeks.
products.bestFor: Living rooms that want a light, linen look with a darkening coating.
pros: Ivory face keeps a room light while the coating blocks sun
104 inch pair width gives good fullness on a standard window
Faux linen texture hides small creases and dust
Thread trimmed finish looks tidy at the seams
cons: White coating can crack if the panel is dried hot
Fabric weight is not stated, so thermal benefit is modest

products.name: MIULEE 52x84 Inch Blackout Linen Curtains, Dusty Blue, 8 Grommets
products.description:
MIULEE uses a triple weave technology, where a middle black layer sits between two face layers, in a 52 by 84 inch panel with eight grommets in a dusty blue. The listing says it blocks light, insulates and works in bedrooms and living rooms.

A triple weave is a stable way to make a blackout without a coating, which means the panel can flex and wash without cracking. Color is a plus: dusty blue is a softer alternative to gray and works with warm woods. Compared with the NICETOWN, the MIULEE is lighter and less heavily lined, so it is better for a living room than a media room. Fabric weight is not stated in the data reviewed.

Eight grommets give a clean fold pattern, and the rod should be at least as wide as the pair. Wash gently. Dusty blue can fade in a sunny window, so check the side facing the glass after a year. If the blue looks different from the photo, test it against a sample of your wall color by holding a panel up before cutting any packaging.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms and living rooms that want a soft color with a woven blackout.
pros: Triple weave blocks light without a coating that can crack
Dusty blue is a softer alternative to gray or black
Eight grommets per panel create even folds
Thermal lining helps with winter drafts
cons: Lighter than the heaviest sets here, so sound dampening is limited
Dusty blue can fade on the side facing strong sun

products.name: Simplebrand 96 Inch Black Blackout Grommet Curtains, 280 GSM
products.description:
Simplebrand makes a pair of 52 by 96 inch panels in 280 gsm black fabric with grommets, and the listing cites an eco-friendly and blackout rate certification. A 96 inch length suits an eight-foot ceiling with the rod set higher than the window, which makes the window look taller.

A 280 gsm weight is a respectable middle ground: it hangs well without needing the heavy hardware of a 340 gsm set. Compared with the NICETOWN, the Simplebrand is lighter and longer, which gives more drop at a smaller weight penalty. The thermal claim should be read as modest, since a lined panel slows heat transfer but does not seal a window.

Hang the rod high and wide, and leave the hem about half an inch above the floor. Wash on a gentle cycle and air dry. Keep black panels away from direct sun if you want to avoid fading on the face. On windows with deep frames, mount the rod on the wall rather than inside the recess so the panels clear the glass when open.
products.bestFor: Rooms with taller ceilings that want a longer drop at a moderate fabric weight.
pros: 96 inch length reaches the floor from a rod mounted high above the frame
280 gsm weight hangs well and blocks most light
Grommets glide on a rod and give even pleats
Black panels make a deep, dark backdrop for a media room
cons: Black fabric shows lint and dust and can fade in strong sun
Thermal benefit is modest and does not replace sealing a window

products.name: Yakamok Natural Linen Textured Blackout Curtains, 84 Inch
products.description:
Yakamok sells a pair of faux linen textured panels, each 52 by 84 inches, in a natural color with a blackout function. The listing says the fabric is soft and finely made.

Natural linen texture suits Scandinavian and farmhouse rooms and pairs well with wood floors and white walls. Faux linen with a blackout coating is heavier than a true linen sheer, so it will not billow, but it wrinkles in transit. Against the MIULEE, the Yakamok has a more neutral color and less color risk, but the data reviewed does not state the weave or the fabric weight.

Hang panels wide enough to be fully drawn across the window, and steam them once after unboxing. Keep them away from heat vents, which can warp coatings. Vacuum the surface lightly and spot clean marks with a damp cloth. Because natural tones read differently by lamp and daylight, hang one panel first and look at it in both before opening the second set.
products.bestFor: Neutral rooms that want a textured, natural look with a blackout function.
pros: Natural linen texture suits wood floors and light walls
Blackout function darkens a bedroom or media room
Pair of 52 by 84 inch panels gives standard fullness
Neutral color is easy to pair with a rug and sofa
cons: Fabric weight and weave type are not stated in the data reviewed
Faux linen wrinkles in transit and needs steaming

buyingCriteria.explanation: Measured in grams per square meter, heavier fabric hangs straighter, blocks more light and mutes sound a little. The NICETOWN lists 340 gsm and the Simplebrand 280 gsm. A heavy panel needs a stronger rod, and a panel without a stated weight, like the Yakamok, is harder to judge.

Panel width should be 1.5 to 2.5 times the window width. A 104 inch pair, as the H.VERSAILTEX offers, fits a window up to about 70 inches wide with good fullness. A flat panel looks skimpy and leaks light at the sides.

Standard lengths are 63, 84, 96 and 108 inches. Hang the rod 4 to 6 inches above the frame and let the hem hover about half an inch above the floor. A 96 inch panel such as the Simplebrand suits an eight-foot ceiling, and the 108 inch H.VERSAILTEX suits taller rooms. If you are unsure, hang the rod slightly higher than seems necessary, because it is easier to raise a rod's look than to lengthen a short panel.
A coating blocks light but can crack, while a triple weave like the MIULEE's is more flexible. Even a true blackout leaks around the edges unless the panel is wide and mounted close to the wall.

Grommet tops glide on a rod and fold evenly, which suits the NICETOWN and Simplebrand. A 1 inch rod bows past 48 inches without a center bracket. Heavy panels need studs or anchors, not light drywall screws.
A $100 cap buys longer lengths, heavier fabrics and wider panels than the entry tier. It still does not buy custom width or lined drapery. For wide bay windows, consider custom or a double rod.

specDecoder.meaning: Grams per square meter, a measure of fabric weight. It indicates body, not quality on its own.
specDecoder.watchFor: The NICETOWN lists 340 and the Simplebrand 280, while the Yakamok lists none.

specDecoder.meaning: Two face layers around a dark middle layer that blocks light without a coating. It is more flexible than a coated fabric.
specDecoder.watchFor: The MIULEE uses it, so check edge leaks around the window.

specDecoder.meaning: A metal or plastic ring in a hole along the top. It lets the panel glide on a rod and folds evenly.
specDecoder.watchFor: The MIULEE has eight per panel, so match the rod diameter to the ring size.

specDecoder.meaning: A lined fabric that slows heat transfer. It does not seal a window or replace weatherstripping.
specDecoder.watchFor: The NICETOWN and Simplebrand claim it, so expect a modest benefit.

specDecoder.meaning: Total width of both panels together. It sets how much fullness you get.
specDecoder.watchFor: The H.VERSAILTEX ivory pair is 104 inches, and the double-wide panel is 100 inches alone.

howWeEvaluated.title: Under cap only
howWeEvaluated.description: Every curtain set here was at or under the cap on its live listing when this guide was updated. Prices move, so recheck before buying. Items above the cap were excluded.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and size
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated fabric weights, such as the NICETOWN's 340 gsm, and panel sizes from 52 by 84 to 100 by 108 inches. Missing specs are labeled as not stated.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blackout method
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each listing for coating or weave type and thermal claims. We do not test products and treat blackout claims as manufacturer statements.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at general themes in owner feedback, such as light leaks at the edges and coatings cracking in dryers. We treat those as patterns, not measurements.

howWeEvaluated.title: Overlap control
howWeEvaluated.description: A lower cap guide on this site covers thinner, shorter panels. We reused none of its picks and favored the upper band of this cap, so this guide is about what the extra budget buys.

cards.label: Coated
cards.text: The H.VERSAILTEX uses a coating that blocks light well but can crack if overheated or machine dried hot.

cards.label: Triple weave
cards.text: The MIULEE blocks light with a woven layer that flexes and washes better, but is slightly less opaque in strong sun.

howToChoose.note: Choose a coating for maximum darkness and a triple weave if you plan to wash often.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A blackout weave, a heavy fabric weight and a width that covers the window with fullness. Mount the rod high and wide to close side gaps.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The NICETOWN and Simplebrand fit best. The NICETOWN is heavier, and the Simplebrand has more length.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a wide bay window, need a lined or interlined drape, custom width or a motorized track.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The window is standard and the room is a bedroom or office. The NICETOWN covers the basics.

maintenance.why: Dust and oils dull the fabric. Use a gentle cycle and air dry so the coating does not crack.
Heat from an iron can damage a coating. A steamer relaxes creases safely.
Heavy panels loosen anchors. Tighten before a bracket pulls from the wall.
Dust collects on the fabric. A soft brush attachment lifts it.
Sun fades the side facing the glass. Swapping the left and right panel evens the fade.

faq.q: Are blackout curtains really 100 percent dark?
faq.a: They block most light through the fabric, but light leaks around the edges and over the rod. Wide panels hung close to the wall reduce it.
Between 1.5 and 2.5 times the window width. A pair of 52 inch panels suits a window up to about 70 inches wide.
Prices move. The cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, so recheck before buying.
They slow heat loss a little, but they do not replace sealing a window. Expect a modest benefit.

faq.q: How do I hang curtains to look taller?
faq.a: Mount the rod 4 to 6 inches above the frame and extend it past the sides so the glass is clear.

faq.q: Can I machine wash blackout curtains?
faq.a: Most can be washed gently, but coatings crack in hot dryers. Check the label and air dry.
